feedback.finish: A microorganism is a very tiny organism that can only be seen through a microscope. Microorganisms that cause diseases are more commonly called germs.

instruction.text: Listen to the statements and decide which one is correct.

b.sound: Bacteria are some of the smallest living things.
Bacteria are some of the largest living things.

feedback.finish: Like many microorganisms, bacteria are only made up of one cell.

instruction.text: Select all the places that contain bacteria.

feedback.finish: There are millions of different types of bacteria, and each one has its own purpose!

instruction.text: Are these actions carried out by good or bad bacteria?

feedback.finish: A specific type of good bacteria called decomposers are found in soil. They break down dead animals and plant matter so that it can be used by other plants for nutrients. This helps to keep plant life healthy.
Some bad bacteria produce acids that attack the outer layer of teeth. If they cause holes in this outer layer, it can lead to tooth decay.
Fermentation caused by some good bacteria helps to turn milk into yoghurt and cheese.
Bad bacteria can enter the body in various  ways, such as through our mouth and eyes. Once inside the body, they reproduce quickly and make us ill.

atoms.a: breaking down food in the gut

feedback.finish: Good bacteria in the body, such as those in the gut, keep us healthy. They help us to digest food and protect us against infections.
